posts.text:
The Learjet 60 crash in Florida is particularly chilling to examine. What was supposed to be a routine private flight from Texas to the Bahamas went wrong the moment the crew encountered severe turbulence and significant icing.

After requesting a climb to find smoother air, the aircraft suddenly entered an extreme overspeed condition. Cockpit audio captures the pilots’ disbelief as the jet rolled into a steep right-hand dive, descending at more than 30,000 feet per minute. 📉

Dashcam footage and radar data show the plane hitting the ground in Palm Beach County at nearly Mach 1 — far beyond the structural limits of any civilian business jet. Early analyses point to a possible structural failure, specifically of the horizontal stabilizer, which would have made recovery impossible. ✈️

Once an aircraft loses pitch trim control at those speeds, aerodynamic forces take over and leave the crew with virtually no chance of recovery.

🚨Casemiro on his conversation with Michael Carrick that convinced him to leave Manchester United:

🗣️ Casemiro: “Honestly, it wasn’t an easy decision. I had a good season, I felt physically strong, I was enjoying my football again and I believed I could still contribute a lot to this team.

“I wasn’t looking for a way out. I wanted to understand where the club was going and whether I was going to be part of its future.

“The conversation with Michael Carrick was what really made me think.

“I remember sitting down with him and asking, ‘Michael, what is the plan for this team? Where do you see Manchester United in the next two or three years, and what are we actually building?’

“He spoke about his ideas, the players he wanted to develop and the changes he believed were necessary. I listened because I respect him.

“But then I asked him, ‘Are we building a team to compete for the Premier League and Champions League, or are we still trying to build a team that can finish in the top four?’

“He looked at me and said, ‘Casemiro, I want to win everything. But there are things at this club that even the manager cannot control.’

“That answer stayed with me.

“I asked what he meant, and he explained that decisions above the manager, including transfers, investment and the club’s structure, would determine how far his plans could go.

“He told me, ‘You can have the best ideas in the world, but if the club doesn’t give you the tools to execute them, you will always have limitations.’

“I understood him because I’ve played for Real Madrid. I know what it means to be at a club where the expectation is to compete for every trophy.

“After that conversation, I started looking beyond the manager and the dressing room. I looked at the club’s foundation, its ownership and the people making the biggest decisions.

“Honestly, I wasn’t convinced. I felt the owners were not ambitious enough for a club of Manchester United’s size.

“You cannot ask players to have the mentality of champions when the entire structure around them isn’t showing the same ambition. Winning must be the objective at every level.

“I remember asking myself, ‘If I stay here for another two years, will I be fighting for the biggest trophies, or will I still be waiting for the club to get everything right?’

“I love Manchester United. I love the supporters, the atmosphere at Old Trafford and everything this badge represents. But I don’t want to spend another season waiting for promises to become reality.

“Some people might think I left because I was no longer good enough or because I was worried about competition. That isn’t true. I had a good season, and I still believe I can compete at the highest level.

“I wasn’t asking for guaranteed minutes or special treatment. I wanted to know that the club was serious about building a team capable of winning major trophies.

“Michael was honest with me, and I respect him. I don’t blame him. A manager can only do so much when the structure above him isn’t moving in the same direction.

“Eventually, I realised this wasn’t just about leaving Manchester United. It was about deciding what I wanted the final years of my career to look like.

“I didn’t want to leave with anger. I won trophies, experienced incredible moments and played in front of supporters who showed me so much love.

“Manchester United is too big to be satisfied with simply becoming competitive again. This club should be fighting for the Premier League and Champions League every season.

“I hope they get there because the supporters deserve it. But I couldn’t keep waiting for that ambition to become reality. I still want to win, and I want my next chapter to be about lifting trophies, not waiting for a project to come together.”
